capabilities: Edit markdown files in a gingko-like tree interface
Open files via the ribbon icon, file context menu, or command palette
Export files from the view context menu
disambiguation: Not a genealogy or family-tree tool; the name refers to a column-based writing layout inspired by Gingko Writer.
problem: Obsidian's default editors show one note as a single document, with no built-in way to write in a branching, column-based structure.
summary: Tree-column writing interface that lets you edit markdown files in a gingko-like layout inside Obsidian.
